statements.text: TranCs can direct DNA cleavage using CRISPR RNAs as well as transposon-derived right-end RNAs.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: TranCs utilize both CRISPR RNAs and reRNAs to direct DNA cleavage.
statements.note: The abstract states directly that TranCs use both RNA types as guides.

statements.text: In LaTranC the guide RNA stays a single reRNA molecule instead of being divided into two parts.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: unlike a single-molecule reRNA, the LaTranC guide RNA is functionally split into a tracrRNA and crRNA
statements.note: The abstract reports the opposite: the LaTranC guide is split into tracrRNA and crRNA.

statements.text: TranC-carrying elements transpose more frequently than TnpB-only elements of the same lineages.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We identify TranCs (transposon-CRISPR intermediates) derived from distinct IS605- or IS607-TnpB lineages.
statements.note: TranC lineages are identified, but no transposition or mobility rates are measured.

statements.text: Engineering a split into the ISDra2 TnpB guide RNA made the nuclease active with a CRISPR array.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: An engineered RNA split of ISDra2 TnpB enabled activity with a CRISPR array.
statements.note: This engineered result is reported as stated.

statements.text: miR-29a-3p levels in plasma extracellular vesicles were compared between smokers and non-smokers with NSCLC.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Prognostic significance was established for miR-29a-3p , showing lower expression in NSCLC patients with disease progression compared to stable disease ( p = 0.004)
statements.note: The only patient comparison reported is progression versus stable disease; smoking status never appears.

statements.text: miR-29a-3p expression was lower in NSCLC patients with disease progression than in those with stable disease, at p = 0.004.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: showing lower expression in NSCLC patients with disease progression compared to stable disease ( p = 0.004)
statements.note: The value and direction match the reported comparison.

statements.text: Patients under-expressing miR-29a-3p had significantly shorter overall survival in Kaplan-Meier analysis (p = 0.038).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: patients with miR-29a-3p under-expression had significantly shorter overall survival (OS) ( p = 0.038)
statements.note: Reported exactly, including the p value.

statements.text: lncRNA H19 was readily detected in plasma extracellular vesicles, where its level tracked disease progression.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Despite the expression of lncRNA H19 in plasma EVs being undetected, its expression in plasma cfRNAs correlated significantly with disease progression ( p = 0.035)
statements.note: H19 was undetected in EVs; the progression correlation came from plasma cfRNAs.

statements.text: Patients with high baseline cfDNA had a median overall survival of 13.0 months against 33.1 months in the low group.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: High-cfDNA independently predicted shorter OS (median 13.0 vs. 33.1 months; p = 0.0015)
statements.note: Both medians are reported as given.

statements.text: High CD86 methylation was independently associated with durable response, with an odds ratio of 6.96.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: high CD86 methylation was independently associated with DR (odds ratio: 6.96, 95% confidence interval: 1.70-28.50; p = 0.0071)
statements.note: The multivariate odds ratio is reported as stated.

statements.text: Serial cfDNA measurement detected progression earlier than radiological imaging did.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In a discovery cohort (n = 17), targeted mutation and methylation profiling on baseline and progression cfDNA was performed.
statements.note: Progression samples were profiled, but cfDNA timing is never compared with imaging.

statements.text: Targeted mutation profiling of baseline cfDNA produced several markers predictive of durable response.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Mutation analysis yielded no predictive markers.
statements.note: The abstract reports that mutation analysis gave no predictive markers at all.

statements.text: Most genes of the two ethnovarieties fall into ethnovariety-specific orthogroups rather than shared ones.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Most genes belong to shared orthogroups, indicating a largely conserved gene repertoire.
statements.note: The abstract reports most genes in shared orthogroups, the reverse of this claim.

statements.text: Roughly 78% of each assembly consists of repetitive DNA, shaped mainly by LTR retrotransposons.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with approximately 78% of their assemblies composed of repetitive DNA largely shaped by LTR retrotransposons
statements.note: The percentage and the dominant element class are both stated.

statements.text: Alkaloid content differs between the caupuri and tucunaca ethnovarieties.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The species encompasses culturally recognized ethnovarieties, some differing in stem architecture.
statements.note: Only stem architecture is mentioned; no chemical measurement of either ethnovariety is reported.

statements.text: Each of the two assemblies resolves into ten chromosome-scale pseudomolecules, spanning 1.16 and 1.13 Gb.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: assemblies span 1.16 and 1.13 Gb, respectively, each organized into ten high-quality chromosome-scale pseudomolecules
statements.note: Sizes and pseudomolecule count are reported as given.

statements.text: A baseline ctDNA fraction of at least 5% was significantly associated with both shorter rPFS and shorter overall survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A ctDNA fraction of at least 5%, as well as TP53 alteration, PTEN alteration, and cell cycle pathway alterations at baseline were significantly associated with shorter rPFS and OS.
statements.note: The threshold and both endpoints are reported as stated.

statements.text: ctDNA profiling identified patients who benefit more from 223Ra than from taxane chemotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study suggests the clinical utility of ctDNA profiling as both a prognostic and a monitoring tool in patients with bone mCRPC treated with 223 Ra.
statements.note: All patients received 223Ra; no alternative treatment was compared.

statements.text: Changes in ctDNA fraction between baseline and end of treatment showed no relationship with rPFS or OS.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Dynamic changes in ctDNA fraction and PTEN alteration between baseline and EOT correlated with distinct rPFS and OS.
statements.note: Dynamic changes did correlate with distinct rPFS and OS.

statements.text: Of 93 patients, ctDNA was profiled in 84 baseline and 74 end-of-treatment samples, with 68 patients matched.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Of 93 patients analyzed, ctDNA was successfully profiled in 84 baseline and 74 EOT samples, with matched data available for 68 patients.
statements.note: All four counts are reported as given.

statements.text: JAK inhibition controls the immune dysregulation caused by the germline STAT3 p.R278H variant.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Immunomodulatory therapies, including cyclosporin A and tacrolimus, controlled autoimmune symptoms in the proband, whereas the parent was refractory to conventional treatments, ultimately succumbing after unsuccessful hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
statements.note: Only cyclosporin A, tacrolimus and transplantation are described; JAK inhibition is never tested.

statements.text: Serum cytokine levels in the proband were reduced, matching the lowered IL1B and TNF transcript levels.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: but diminished cytokine transcripts ( IL1B, TNF ). Serum cytokines, however, were markedly elevated, highlighting discordant transcriptional and translational regulation.
statements.note: Serum cytokines were markedly elevated despite the diminished transcripts.

statements.text: Single-cell sequencing of the proband showed marked CD8+ T-cell expansion with raised STAT3 and STAT1 expression.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Single-cell transcriptomics revealed marked expansion of CD8 + T cells in the proband, accompanied by altered expression of JAK/STAT pathway genes, including elevated STAT3, STAT 1
statements.note: Both the expansion and the elevated pathway genes are reported.

statements.text: Cyclosporin A and tacrolimus controlled the proband's autoimmune symptoms, while the parent was refractory to conventional treatment.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Immunomodulatory therapies, including cyclosporin A and tacrolimus, controlled autoimmune symptoms in the proband, whereas the parent was refractory to conventional treatments
statements.note: The contrasting treatment courses are stated directly.

statements.text: dMMR-associated signatures were common among subclonal mutations in HCC but absent from noncancerous liver tissue.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: dMMR-associated signatures were commonly observed in subclonal mutations in HCC, but were absent in noncancerous liver tissues.
statements.note: Reported as stated in the first analysis.

statements.text: A high proportion of dMMR-associated signatures went together with reduced expression of mismatch repair genes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: lower expression of the IL6 gene, but not with decreased expression of mismatch repair genes
statements.note: The association with decreased mismatch repair gene expression was explicitly absent.

statements.text: The first analysis drew on multi-regional whole-genome sequencing of 529 samples from 26 patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we performed mutational signature analyses across various stages of hepatocarcinogenesis using multi-regional whole-genome sequencing data from 529 samples from 26 patients with or without HCC
statements.note: Both counts match the reported dataset.

statements.text: Tumours with a high proportion of dMMR-associated signatures carry a higher neoantigen load.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The third analysis showed that a high proportion of dMMR-associated signatures were significantly associated with better response rates and longer progression-free survival.
statements.note: Better immunotherapy outcomes are reported, but neoantigen or mutation burden is never measured.

statements.text: Tumour mutation burden in the kinase-associated spindle cell tumours was consistently high.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Tumor mutation burden was consistently low, with CDKN2A homozygous deletion being the only recurrent secondary event (4/5 cases profiled).
statements.note: The abstract reports consistently low tumour mutation burden.

statements.text: Patients whose tumours carried BRAF fusions responded to MEK or RAF inhibitor treatment.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Among the five patients with follow-up (median 34 months), one patient died of disease, with two developing local recurrences at 5 and 84 months.
statements.note: Follow-up outcomes are given, but no targeted therapy was administered or assessed.

statements.text: Of the 24 BRAF fusion cases identified, 18 (75%) arose in histotypes already recognised as BRAF-driven.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified a total of 24 cases harboring BRAF fusions, with 18 (75%) occurring in canonical BRAF-driven histotypes
statements.note: The count and percentage are reported as given.

statements.text: In the kinase-associated spindle cell tumours the BRAF breakpoints fell in exons 8-11, leaving the kinase domain intact.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: BRAF breakpoints clustered in exons 8-11 retaining an intact kinase domain
statements.note: The breakpoint range and intact kinase domain are stated.

statements.text: With a typical 33 ng cfDNA input the practical detection limit was about 0.01% mutant allele frequency.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: when analyzing cfDNA from plasma with a typical input of 33 ng, the practical detection limit was ~10 -4 or 0.01% mutant allele frequency (MAF)
statements.note: Input amount and practical limit are reported as given.

statements.text: In 17 of the 19 patients whose tumour DNA carried hotspot mutations, at least one was found in plasma at diagnosis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In 17 of 19 patients with identified hotspot mutations in tumor gDNA, at least one hotspot mutation could be detected in plasma DNA at the time of diagnosis.
statements.note: The proportion is reported exactly.

statements.text: Mutant allele frequency fell across follow-up time points in the four patients who relapsed clinically.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The MAF increased at subsequent time points in four of the patients who experienced a clinical relapse.
statements.note: MAF increased rather than fell in those patients.

statements.text: Plasma analysis flagged relapse earlier than clinical or imaging diagnosis in these colorectal cancer patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In conclusion, multiplex superRCA assays proved suitable for monitoring CRC patients by analyzing hotspot mutations in cfDNA, and dynamic changes in MAF were observed in patients with clinical relapse.
statements.note: Rising MAF in relapsing patients is reported, but detection timing is never compared.

statements.text: The BCNN model detects ctDNA in gastric and colorectal cancer plasma as accurately as in ESCC.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our study uses enzymatic method to detect whole genome abnormal methylation regions in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).
statements.note: Only ESCC samples were analysed; no other tumour type was tested.

statements.text: The BCNN reached an AUC of 0.970 for identifying ctDNA, the best of the models compared.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Compared to traditional models, our BCNN demonstrates the best performance in identifying ctDNA (AUC = 0.970).
statements.note: The AUC and the comparison with traditional models are stated.

statements.text: The enzymatic whole-genome methylation protocol recovered fewer CpG sites than the bisulfite-based method.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: enzyme-based whole-genome methylation sequencing retained more longer cfDNA and detected more CpG sites than bisulfite-based method in both gDNA and cfDNA
statements.note: The enzymatic method detected more CpG sites, not fewer.

statements.text: At 93.75% specificity in the validation cohort, 7 of 8 stage I ESCC cases were called positive.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: in the validation cohort, when the specificity is 93.75%, 7 out of 8 early-stage ESCC (TNM Stage I) were identified as positive in our preliminary results
statements.note: Specificity and the 7 of 8 result are reported as given.

statements.text: Repeat content reaches 54.3% in S. oregonense against at least 15.7% in P. mocquerysi.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Repeat content is higher in S. oregonense than in P. mocquerysi, 54.3% against a lower bound of 15.7%.
statements.note: Both figures, including the lower bound, are reported as given.

statements.text: Expression of the expanded carboxylesterase genes is highest in larvae.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: with notable expansions in several gene families including carboxylesterases, serine proteases, and lipid metabolism genes in Amblyoponinae
statements.note: Gene-family expansions come from genome comparison; no expression data for any life stage are shown.

statements.text: The S. oregonense assembly is the larger of the two at 262 Mb and the more fragmented, with 1,189 scaffolds.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we assembled the P. mocquerysi genome (187 Mb, 307 scaffolds, N50 = 5.26 Mb, BUSCO 99.2% complete) and the S. oregonense genome (262 Mb, 1,189 scaffolds, N50 = 0.84 Mb, BUSCO 98.3% complete)
statements.note: Sizes and scaffold counts are reported as given.

statements.text: The repeat-content gap between the two ant genomes lies mostly in well-classified LTR retrotransposon families.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Most of the difference is in unclassified repeats, which we show to be diverged transposable elements.
statements.note: The difference is attributed to unclassified, diverged repeats.

statements.text: Sequenza performed well on low-coverage samples carrying few copy number alterations.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Sequenza can only perform well in high-coverage and more-CNA samples.
statements.note: Sequenza performed well only with high coverage and more CNAs.

statements.text: At 5X coverage ControlFreeC performed well only when tumour purity was above 50%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: For coverage=5X samples, ControlFreeC requires tumor purity to be above 50% to perform well.
statements.note: The coverage and purity condition are stated directly.

statements.text: Across the simulated settings tested, Accucopy gave the best overall performance of the three callers.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Under the settings tested (sequencing depth at 5X or 30X, purity from 0.1 to 0.9, existence of subclones or not), Accucopy is the best-performing algorithm overall.
statements.note: Reported as the third main result.

statements.text: Runtime and memory use differ substantially among the three algorithms.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Therefore, we selected three algorithms: Accucopy, Sequenza , and ControlFreeC , and applied them to data simulated under different settings.
statements.note: Only detection performance is assessed; computational cost is never reported.

statements.text: The high-depth random forest beat rule-based filtering at every threshold in the test data, with a PR-AUC of 0.71.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Precision-recall curves showed the high depth model outperformed rule-based filtering at all thresholds in Test Data (PR-AUC 0.71).
statements.note: The comparison and PR-AUC are reported as given.

statements.text: The low-depth model was fitted on whole exome cfDNA data sequenced to roughly 500X.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Low depth models were fitted and evaluated on whole exome sequencing (WES) cfDNA data at depths of approximately 10X while the high depth data was sequenced at approximately 500X.
statements.note: The low-depth model used about 10X data; 500X was the high-depth data.

statements.text: Applying the random forest filter changed how many patients were judged eligible for targeted therapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our results demonstrate the utility of supervised ML models for filtering variants in cfDNA data.
statements.note: Only filtering performance is evaluated; no treatment-decision outcome is examined.

statements.text: Presence in COSMIC and absence from dbSNP common variants raised the predicted probability of a true somatic variant.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Partial dependence plots showed membership in the COSMIC database, absence from the dbSNP common variants database, and increasing read depth increased mean probability of high confidence somatic variant prediction in both models.
statements.note: Both features are reported to increase the predicted probability.

statements.text: ST135 isolates formed thicker biofilms than isolates of other sequence types.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Proteus mirabilis is an undercharacterized and challenging UTI pathogen due to intrinsic resistance and biofilm formation.
statements.note: Biofilm formation appears only as background; no biofilm assay or lineage comparison is reported.

statements.text: Sequence typing of the collection found 213 sequence types, only 7% of them represented by ten or more genomes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Multilocus sequence typing (MLST) identified 213 MLSTs, with only 7% having ≥10 genomes, highlighting strain diversity.
statements.note: Both numbers are reported as given.

statements.text: In the multidrug-resistant ST135 lineage, 95% of genomes carried at least 16 resistance genes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ST135 was identified as a highly MDR lineage, with 95% of genomes carrying ≥16 resistance genes.
statements.note: Reported exactly for ST135.

statements.text: Genotype matched phenotype for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and chloramphenicol, while kanamycin predictions were discordant.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: While the presence of genes like aph(3')-la reliably predicted kanamycin resistance, discordance for antibiotics such as trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and chloramphenicol revealed that AMR gene stacking
statements.note: The pattern is the reverse: kanamycin was reliably predicted, the other two were discordant.

statements.text: The k-mer genome size estimates fall far below the 4.56 Gbp measured for the same species by flow cytometry.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our GS estimates are well below the GS (= 4.56 Gbp) determined for the same species using flow cytometry.
statements.note: The discrepancy and the flow cytometry value are stated.

statements.text: Among annotated transposable elements LINEs were most abundant at 12.64%, ahead of DNA transposons and LTR elements.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Among annotated transposable elements, Long Interspersed Nuclear Elements (LINEs, 12.64%), DNA transposons (7.35%), and Long Terminal Repeats (LTRs, 5.44%) were the most common.
statements.note: The ranking and percentages are reported as given.

statements.text: The mitochondrial genome shows gene order rearrangements relative to other spiny lobsters.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In J. frontalis, the circular mitochondrial genome is 15,514 bp in length and contains 22 transfer (tRNA) genes, 13 PCGs, and two ribosomal RNA genes (12 S and 16 S ribosomal RNA)
statements.note: Length and gene content are given, but mitochondrial gene arrangement is never compared.

statements.text: SINEs were more abundant in the nuclear genome than LINEs.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Less abundant transposable elements included Rolling Circles (1.3%), Short Interspersed Nuclear Elements (SINEs, 0.64%), Satellite DNA (0.43%), and simple repeats (0.42%), among others.
statements.note: SINEs are listed at 0.64%, far below the 12.64% reported for LINEs.

statements.text: Transposon insertions per plant were markedly more numerous in oilseed flax than in fiber flax, mirroring the SNP difference.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Unlike SNPs, which were significantly more numerous in oilseed flax than in fiber flax, we did not find such a substantial difference in the number of insertions of different transposon families per plant among samples of different morphotypes.
statements.note: No substantial morphotype difference in insertion numbers was found, unlike for SNPs.

statements.text: The 50 trait-associated insertions sit inside or near genes whose expression they alter.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: A genome-wide association study (GWAS) identified 50 TE insertions associated with different phenotypic traits, with many associations confirmed by multiple models or detected in data from multiple years.
statements.note: The associations are statistical; no gene-expression or positional analysis of the insertions is reported.

statements.text: The screen found 588,480 transposon insertion sites absent from the reference flax genome, mostly Copia and Gypsy retrotransposons.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We discovered 588,480 new transposon insertion sites not present in the reference flax genome (NCBI assembly ASM22429v2), the majority of which were attributed to retrotransposons of the Copia and Gypsy superfamilies
statements.note: The count and the dominant superfamilies are reported as given.

statements.text: Of 61 candidate regions shaped by recent breeding, 18 overlapped QTLs for important agronomic traits.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Analysis of genomic regions affected by recent breeding efforts revealed a total of 61 candidate regions, of which 18 regions overlapped with QTLs associated with important agronomic traits.
statements.note: Both counts are reported exactly.

statements.text: The two monokaryon assemblies differ by 1.17 Mb (30.87 versus 32.04 Mb), attributed mainly to transposable element expansion in PP85.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Comparative genomic analysis revealed a genome size difference of 1.17 Mb (30.87 vs. 32.04 Mb), primarily attributed to transposable element (TE) expansion in strain PP85.
statements.note: Sizes and the attributed cause are reported as given.

statements.text: Fruiting body yield in cultivation is higher for PP85 than for PP78.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Phlebopus portentosus is a widely consumed edible mushroom and the only Boletales species currently cultivated on an industrial scale.
statements.note: Cultivation appears only as background; no yield or fruiting data for either monokaryon are given.

statements.text: Terpenoid biosynthetic clusters were expanded in this fungus while the polyketide synthase pathways contracted.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The expansion of non-ribosomal peptide synthetase and polyketide synthase pathways, alongside contraction of terpenoid clusters typical of ECM fungi, further indicated its adaptation to saprotroph.
statements.note: The directions are reversed: polyketide pathways expanded and terpenoid clusters contracted.

statements.text: Annotation found 187 genes unique to PP78 and 236 unique to PP85, the latter enriched for TE-related and putative virulence functions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Functional annotation identified 187 PP78-specific and 236 PP85-specific genes, with the latter enriched in TE-related and putative virulence factors.
statements.note: Both counts and the enrichment are reported as given.

statements.text: The assemblies each contain four nuclear chromosomes and together resolved 118 of 120 telomeres.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Each genome was assembled into four nuclear chromosomes, with 118 of 120 telomeres resolved
statements.note: Chromosome count and resolved telomeres are reported as given.

statements.text: Transposable element content varied widely between the Brazilian isolates, alongside several chromosome-scale rearrangements.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The genomes are structurally conserved, showing no chromosome-scale rearrangements and uniform transposable element content.
statements.note: TE content was uniform and no chromosome-scale rearrangements were seen.

statements.text: Orthology analysis assigned 90.4% of genes to the core genome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Orthology assignment placed 90.4% of genes in the core genome.
statements.note: The percentage is reported exactly.

statements.text: Deoxynivalenol production differs among the fifteen sequenced isolates.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This suggests that the large phenotypic variance in aggressiveness observed between isolates likely resides in regulatory differences and/or within the small and largely uncharacterised accessory fraction.
statements.note: Aggressiveness variance is referred to, but no mycotoxin or metabolite measurements appear.

statements.text: Patients with high TRPRS had larger tumour volumes at diagnosis.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Differential expression analysis across clinical variables in The Cancer Genome Atlas Glioblastoma cohort (TCGA-GBM; n = 529) identified 193 TRP-associated genes significantly linked to patient outcomes.
statements.note: Clinical variables were used for gene selection, but tumour size or volume is never reported.

statements.text: The seven-gene TRPRS split patients by overall survival in all four datasets, with AUCs of 0.72 to 0.81.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: TRPRS robustly stratified GBM patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly distinct overall survival across all four datasets (AUC = 0.72-0.81).
statements.note: The AUC range and the four datasets are reported as given.

statements.text: High-TRPRS tumours were the ones frequently carrying TP53 mutations and 1q21.3 deletions.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: high-TRPRS tumors were enriched for PTEN loss and 9q21.3 amplification, whereas low-TRPRS tumors frequently harbored TP53 mutations and 1q21.3 deletions
statements.note: TP53 mutations and 1q21.3 deletions were features of low-TRPRS tumours.

statements.text: Knocking down IFNGR2 reduced glioma cell proliferation and dampened NF-kB signalling in vitro.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Functional assays demonstrated that IFNGR2 knockdown suppressed glioma cell proliferation and attenuated NF- κ B signaling
statements.note: Both effects of the knockdown are reported.

statements.text: The prophage deletant of R20291 remained resistant to infection by the phage it had lost.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The R20291 ϕ027 deletant was sensitive to ϕ027 infection
statements.note: The deletant was sensitive to infection, not resistant.

statements.text: Deleting the transposon from strain 630 left PaLoc transfer frequency unchanged at 1 x 10-7.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The 630 Tn 5397 deletant transferred PaLoc at the same frequency (1 × 10 -7 ) as 630 harboring Tn 5397
statements.note: The transfer frequency and the equivalence with the parent strain are stated.

statements.text: The prophage deletant produced less toxin than the wild type strain.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Growth kinetics of R20291 ϕ027 deletant was similar to wild type (WT) in rich medium but marginally reduced compared with WT in minimal medium.
statements.note: Only growth was compared with wild type; toxin production was not measured.

statements.text: The prophage deletion produced the largest deleted locus so far described in C. difficile, at 56.8 kb.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: resulting in the largest deleted locus (56.8 kb) described in C. difficile
statements.note: The size and the claim of being the largest are stated.

statements.text: More than 78% of the assembly is transposable elements, and 94% of those carry repeat-induced point mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified 14,145 genes and over 78% of the genome consists of transposable elements (TEs). Of these, 94% are affected by repeat-induced point mutations (RIP)
statements.note: Both proportions are reported as given.

statements.text: Three TE families, Ty3, Ty1 and Tad1, together account for over 60% of genome size.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with three TE families (Ty3, Ty1, and Tad1) contributing over 60% of the genome size
statements.note: The families and their combined share are stated.

statements.text: Fewer TEs were differentially expressed between sclerotia and free-living mycelium than between ectomycorrhizal and free-living mycelium.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we found 56 TEs differentially transcribed between ectomycorrhizal and free-living mycelium tissues. An even higher number (n = 66) of TEs were differentially expressed between stress resistance morphology (i.e. sclerotia) and free-living mycelium.
statements.note: The sclerotia comparison gave more differentially expressed TEs (66) than the symbiosis comparison (56).

statements.text: Strains from drier sites carry more TE copies than strains from wetter sites.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Screening of 15 additional C. geophilum strains revealed recent and lineage-specific TE expansions, implying that several TEs escaped the RIP machinery and retained potential activity.
statements.note: Strain screening showed lineage-specific expansions, but strains are not compared by habitat or moisture.

statements.text: The Crn4 orthologues of phages and plasmids are expressed during infection.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Phage and plasmids also encode Crn4 orthologues that may function as anti-CRISPRs.
statements.note: The orthologues were found in genomes; no expression or infection experiment is reported.

statements.text: Crn4 belongs to type I CRISPR systems rather than type III-D systems.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Here, we describe the structure and mechanism of a new family of ring nucleases, Crn4, associated with type III-D CRISPR systems.
statements.note: Crn4 is reported as associated with type III-D systems.

statements.text: Crn4 is a small homodimer whose fold matches no previously described ring nuclease or any known protein structure.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The crystal structure of Crn4 reveals a small homodimeric protein with a fold unrelated to any known ring nuclease or, indeed, any known protein structure.
statements.note: Oligomeric state and the novel fold are stated directly.

statements.text: Crn4 cleaves several cyclic oligoadenylate species to linear oligoadenylates in vitro and weakens type III immunity in vivo.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Crn4 degrades a range of cOA species to linear oligoadenylates in vitro and ameliorates type III CRISPR immunity in vivo
statements.note: Both the in vitro activity and the in vivo effect are reported.

statements.text: The gene-family expansions seen in the laboratory strain reflect genuine copy-number gains rather than assembly artefacts.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: whereas apparent expansions in the laboratory strain largely reflect annotation inflation arising from assembly fragmentation
statements.note: Those expansions are attributed to annotation inflation from fragmented assembly.

statements.text: The resurrected genome contains about 38% repetitive DNA, roughly 1.8 times the proportion in the laboratory strain.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The resurrected genome harbors ∼38% repetitive DNA approximately 1.8-fold higher than the laboratory strain
statements.note: Both the percentage and the fold difference are reported.

statements.text: Expanded orthogroups in the resurrected strain are enriched for retroelement domains and stress-response families such as small heat shock proteins.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Expanded orthogroups in the resurrected strain are enriched for retroelement-associated domains, nucleic-acid processing functions, and stress-responsive gene families, including small heat shock proteins
statements.note: The enrichment categories are reported as given.

statements.text: The resurrected strain grows faster than the laboratory strain under high salinity.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Here, we present a highly contiguous nuclear genome assembly of Chaetoceros muelleri generated from living cells resurrected from resting spores preserved in Baltic Sea sediments and sequenced using PacBio HiFi long read technology.
statements.note: The resurrected cells were used for sequencing only; no growth or stress experiments are described.

statements.text: ERBB2 amplification was found in 59 of 820 primary bladder cancers (7.4%) and was commonest in micropapillary carcinoma at 19%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ERBB2 amplification was present in 59 (7.4%) of 820 bladder cancers and amplification varied by subtype with amplification most frequently identified in micropapillary carcinoma (19%)
statements.note: Counts, overall rate and the subtype maximum are reported as given.

statements.text: Patients with ERBB2-amplified tumours treated with HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugates had longer survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The introduction of antibody-drug-conjugates (ADC) that target HER2 has renewed interest in ERBB2 alterations in bladder cancer.
statements.note: HER2-targeted conjugates are mentioned as motivation; no treatment or survival outcomes were analysed.

statements.text: Among 209 nodal metastases, 26 (12.4%) were ERBB2-amplified, with a kappa of 0.61 against the matched primary.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ERBB2 amplification occurred in 26 (12.4%) of 209 nodal metastases and there was concordance in amplification between primary and nodal metastases (kappa = 0.61).
statements.note: The count, percentage and kappa are reported exactly.

statements.text: Protein expression was significantly higher in the primary tumours than in their lymph node metastases.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: and the nodal metastases had a significantly higher expression (p < 0.001)
statements.note: Expression was significantly higher in the nodal metastases, not the primaries.

statements.text: Patients whose paired components had divergent copy number profiles had worse overall survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The differences observed in a subset likely reflect earlier divergent evolution of the SM subclones, with CNAs possibly underlying tumor progression.
statements.note: Divergence is interpreted evolutionarily; no patient survival or outcome data are reported.

statements.text: In 8 of 11 tumours (73%) the paired somatic-type and conventional components had similar copy number profiles.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In most tumors (8/11; 73%), CNA profiles of the paired samples were similar.
statements.note: The proportion is reported exactly.

statements.text: A set of highly recurrent copy number alterations was identified in the somatic-type malignancy components.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: No highly recurrent CNAs were identified in the SM components.
statements.note: The abstract states no highly recurrent alterations were found in those components.

statements.text: In the three tumours whose profiles differed, the somatic-type component carried the greater number of copy number alterations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In the remaining 3 tumors (3/11; 27%), the CNA profiles showed noticeable differences, with a higher number of CNAs in SM.
statements.note: The direction of the difference is reported as given.

statements.text: The att DNA is sharply bent, with an arginine side chain of TnsD inserted into a CC/GG dinucleotide step.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our structures reveal a striking bending of the att DNA, featured by the intercalation of an arginine side chain of TnsD into a CC/GG dinucleotide step.
statements.note: The bending and the intercalating arginine are reported as given.

statements.text: TnsD binds the attachment site but does not recruit the TnsABC proteins, which assemble independently.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Recognition of the attachment (att) site by TnsD recruits the TnsABC proteins to form the transpososome and facilitate transposition.
statements.note: Recognition by TnsD is what recruits TnsABC.

statements.text: Besides recruiting TnsAB, TnsC takes part directly in assembling the transpososome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: demonstrates that TnsC not only recruits TnsAB but also directly participates in the transpososome assembly
statements.note: Both roles of TnsC are stated.

statements.text: Mutating the intercalating arginine of TnsD abolished transposition.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings provide mechanistic insights into targeted DNA insertion by Tn7-like transposons, with implications for improving the precision and efficiency of their genome-editing applications.
statements.note: The work is structural; no mutational or transposition assays are described.

statements.text: Older recipient age went with higher first dd-cfDNA% in the unadjusted analysis.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Higher first dd-cfDNA% was associated with larger BSA ratio (p = 0.039), BSA ratio ≥ 1.5 (median 0.17% vs. 0.06%, p = 0.0185), larger weight ratio (p = 0.016), LV mass oversizing (median 0.17% vs. 0.06%, p = 0.0196), and younger age (p = 0.008).
statements.note: Younger, not older, age was associated with higher first dd-cfDNA%.

statements.text: Recipients with a donor-to-recipient BSA ratio of at least 1.5 had a median first dd-cfDNA of 0.17% against 0.06%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: BSA ratio ≥ 1.5 (median 0.17% vs. 0.06%, p = 0.0185)
statements.note: Both medians and the threshold are reported as given.

statements.text: A higher dd-cfDNA% threshold is needed to flag rejection in recipients of oversized grafts.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These exploratory findings support further investigation of size mismatch, recipient age, and early allograft adaptation as potential non-rejection contributors to dd-cfDNA elevation.
statements.note: Only associations in rejection-free recipients are reported; no diagnostic threshold was evaluated.

statements.text: After adjustment for age, neither size mismatch nor age remained independently associated with the first dd-cfDNA value.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: After age adjustment, neither size mismatch nor age was independently associated with first dd-cfDNA%.
statements.note: Reported exactly as the adjusted result.

statements.text: TE landscapes were characterised in 18 Myrtaceae species, and LTR Class I elements were the main contributors to genome size variation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In our research, we have characterized the landscape of TEs in 18 species of Myrtaceae. Our results showed that LTR Class I elements are the main contributors to genome size variations in Myrtaceae.
statements.note: The species count and the leading element class are reported as given.

statements.text: A horizontal transfer of a Copia/Ivana element was detected between the Syzygieae and Myrteae tribes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A positive HTT of a Copia/Ivana TE among Syzygieae and Myrteae tribes
statements.note: The transfer event and the two tribes are stated.

statements.text: TE content correlates with chromosome number across the species examined.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Most available Myrtaceae genome assemblies are arranged in 11 chromosomes, and possess large variability in genome sizes, sometimes over triple the size.
statements.note: Chromosome number is background only; TE profiles were correlated with climate and distribution data.

statements.text: Coding sequences, rather than transposable elements, are the main contributors to genome size variation in this family.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Although coding sequences add to this disparity, transposable elements (TEs) are the main contributors to genome size variation.
statements.note: Transposable elements are named as the main contributors.

statements.text: The size of the early tumour fraction decline predicted which patients responded to therapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: may correlate with therapy response, but little is known regarding TF dynamics immediately after therapy initiation
statements.note: Response correlation is the motivation; only tumour fraction dynamics, not patient outcomes, were analysed.

statements.text: Tumour fraction fell significantly from pre-infusion to day 9, from 16% to 6.5%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: there was significant decline in TF from pre-infusion to D9 (16% to 6.5%, p = 0.004)
statements.note: Both values and the significance are reported as given.

statements.text: No surge in ctDNA tumour fraction occurred within 24 hours of onalespib, paclitaxel or the combination.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: There was no ctDNA TF surge within minutes to 24 h of onalespib, paclitaxel, or combination, despite an overall decline in TF during the first therapy cycle.
statements.note: The absence of a surge for all three infusions is stated.

statements.text: Tumour fraction rose significantly from pre-infusion to 6 hours after paclitaxel.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: There was significant TF decline from pre-infusion to 6 h for paclitaxel (p = 0.03) but no change for onalespib or onalespib+paclitaxel at 6hl.
statements.note: The 6-hour change after paclitaxel was a significant decline, not a rise.

statements.text: Chromosome 8q gains and amplifications were subclonal in 31% of the tumours carrying them.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: which were not restricted to one of the main subtypes and showed subclonality in 31% of the affected tumours
statements.note: The subclonality percentage is reported as given.

statements.text: Chromosome 8q gains were required for metastatic dissemination in these tumours.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: These tertiary alterations were not required for metastatic dissemination.
statements.note: The abstract states these alterations were not required for dissemination.

statements.text: Subclonal 8q gains were more frequent in larger primary tumours.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Tumour progression was further studied by analysing matched primary and metastatic lesions from five patients.
statements.note: The only tissue comparison is primary versus metastatic; tumour size is never reported.

statements.text: The three evolutionary subtypes defined by EIF1AX mutation, SF3B1 mutation or monosomy 3p were usually mutually exclusive and near-clonal.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: three main evolutionary subtypes could be identified based on having an EIF1AX mutation, SF3B1 mutation or monosomy 3p. These alterations were usually mutually-exclusive and (near-) clonally abundant
statements.note: The subtypes, their exclusivity and clonal abundance are reported as given.

statements.text: MLT2 is the long terminal repeat of the HERVK family.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: This study examines the diversity and evolution of human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) of the HERVL family, which has long terminal repeats (LTRs) named MLT2.
statements.note: MLT2 is given as the long terminal repeat of the HERVL family.

statements.text: Probability-based sequence comparison uncovered systematic annotation errors that mask the diversity of human transposable elements.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: By probability-based sequence comparison, we uncover systematic annotation errors that conceal the true complexity and diversity of transposable elements (TEs) in the human genome.
statements.note: The method and the finding are stated directly.

statements.text: The analysis defines new MLT2 subfamilies and builds new consensus sequences for them.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our analysis identifies new subfamilies within the MLT2 group, proposes a refined classification scheme, and constructs new consensus sequences.
statements.note: Both outputs are reported as given.

statements.text: MLT2 elements are transcribed in human embryonic stem cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We present an evolutionary analysis including phylogenetic trees that elucidate the relationships between these subfamilies and their contributions to human evolution.
statements.note: The work is sequence and phylogeny based; no transcription or cell-type data appear.

statements.text: In 12 of the 18 cancer types studied, at least one signature's activity predicted survival after adjustment for established prognostic factors.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In 12 of 18 studied cancer types, we identified at least one mutational signature whose activity predicted survival outcomes after adjusting for the established prognostic factors.
statements.note: The proportion and the adjustment are reported as given.

statements.text: Patients were grouped by treatment received to test whether signature activity predicted therapy response.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We further explored the prognostic differences according to, for example, the HPV status in head and neck squamous cell carcinomas and smoking status in lung cancers.
statements.note: Subgroups by HPV and smoking status are described; no treatment-response analysis is reported.

statements.text: Signature activity was associated with overall survival in nine cancer types and with disease-specific survival in seven.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: overall survival was associated with the activity of mutational signatures in nine cancer types and disease-specific survival in seven cancer types
statements.note: Both counts are reported exactly.

statements.text: The clock-like signatures SBS5 and SBS40 were the ones least often linked to the survival endpoints.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The clock-like signatures SBS5 and SBS40 were most commonly associated with survival endpoints.
statements.note: They were the most commonly associated signatures, not the least.

statements.text: Restoring SMYD4 expression in tumour cells slows their proliferation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: SMYD4 demonstrated its role as a tumor suppressor in the majority of tumors evaluated.
statements.note: The tumour-suppressor role is inferred from database analyses; no functional experiments are reported.

statements.text: SMYD4 showed heterozygous loss and downregulation in every tumour type evaluated.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In terms of CNAs, SMYD4 consistently exhibited heterozygous loss and downregulation across all tumors evaluated.
statements.note: Reported as a consistent finding across all tumours.

statements.text: Stomach adenocarcinoma was the one tumour type in which SMYD4 expression was lower than in normal tissue.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Moreover, SMYD4 showed low expression in tumor samples compared to normal samples, except for stomach adenocarcinoma.
statements.note: Stomach adenocarcinoma was the exception to the low tumour expression, not the only instance of it.

statements.text: Low SMYD4 expression went with significantly poorer overall survival in stomach and lung adenocarcinoma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: patients with low SMYD4 expression in STAD and LUAD tumors exhibited significantly poorer overall survival
statements.note: Both tumour types and the survival direction are stated.

statements.text: Among 35 patient-derived metastatic organoids, those from pretreated patients carried a higher mutational load and more structural variants.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: comparing 35 patient-derived metastatic organoids (PDOs) from pretreated and chemonaive patients with mCRC. Combining PDO drug sensitivity assessments with RNA and whole genome sequencing, we found PDOs from pretreated patients exhibited higher mutational load and more structural variants.
statements.note: The organoid count and both genomic differences are reported as given.

statements.text: Organoids from oxaliplatin-resistant patients stayed resistant, with ZNF300 and TGM2 upregulation and Hedgehog pathway enrichment.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: PDOs from oxaliplatin-resistant patients maintained this resistance, showing the upregulation of ZNF300 , TGM2 , and Hedgehog pathway enrichment.
statements.note: The retained resistance and the associated changes are stated.

statements.text: Organoid drug sensitivity predicted how the corresponding patients responded to their next line of treatment.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our findings reveal that PDOs capture chemotherapy-induced genomic and phenotypic changes differently depending on the drug
statements.note: Organoids are compared with patients' prior exposure, not with any subsequent clinical response.

statements.text: Acquired resistance to 5-FU and irinotecan was fully reproduced in the organoids.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Acquired resistance to 5-FU and irinotecan was only partially captured
statements.note: That resistance was only partially captured.

statements.text: The integrative analysis drew on transcriptomic data alone, leaving mutation and methylation layers aside.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In this work, we apply integrative multi-omics analysis to explore the interplay between genomic (mutations), epigenomic (DNA methylation), and transcriptomic (mRNA and miRNA) layers.
statements.note: Mutation and methylation layers were part of the integrative analysis.

statements.text: The candidate biomarkers were confirmed in an independent glioma cohort.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our approach relies on Multi-Omics Factor Analysis (MOFA), a Bayesian latent factor analysis model designed to capture sources of variation across different omics types.
statements.note: Only the one multi-omics analysis is described; no external validation cohort is mentioned.

statements.text: The factor analysis separated distinct molecular profiles across the three glioma types.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our results highlight distinct molecular profiles across the three glioma types and identify potential relationships between methylation and genetic expression.
statements.note: Distinct profiles across the three types are reported as a result.

statements.text: The analysis turned up candidate biomarkers with prognostic value and a transcriptional profile tied to neural system development.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we uncover novel candidate biomarkers with prognostic value, as well as a transcriptional profile associated with neural system development
statements.note: Both findings are reported as given.
